passages.text: “I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me. To a nation that did not call My name, I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to a nation that did not know Him.
God revealed Himself to people who did not ask for Him.
God let Himself be found by those who did not seek Him.
God said, “Here I am! Here I am!”
God spoke to a nation that did not call on His name.
passages.original: נִדְרַ֙שְׁתִּי֙ לְל֣וֹא שָׁאָ֔לוּ נִמְצֵ֖אתִי לְלֹ֣א בִקְשֻׁ֑נִי אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ הִנֵּ֣נִי הִנֵּ֔נִי אֶל־ גּ֖וֹי לֹֽא־ קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי׃

passages.text: All day long I have held out My hands to an obstinate people who walk in the wrong path, who follow their own imaginations, to a people who continually provoke Me to My face, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on altars of brick, sitting among the graves, spending nights in secret places, eating the meat of pigs and polluted broth from their bowls.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to His people.
He holds out His hands all day long.
His people are stubborn.
They do not listen to Him.
They walk in the wrong path.
They follow their own thoughts.
They make God angry again and again.
They do this openly, right in front of Him.
They offer sacrifices in gardens.
They burn incense on altars made of brick.
They sit among graves.
They spend the night in secret places.
They eat the meat of pigs.
They fill their bowls with unclean food.
passages.original: פֵּרַ֧שְׂתִּי יָדַ֛י כָּל־ הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל־ עַ֣ם סוֹרֵ֑ר הַהֹלְכִים֙ הַדֶּ֣רֶךְ לֹא־ ט֔וֹב אַחַ֖ר מַחְשְׁבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃ הָעָ֗ם הַמַּכְעִיסִ֥ים אוֹתִ֛י עַל־ פָּנַ֖י תָּמִ֑יד זֹֽבְחִים֙ בַּגַּנּ֔וֹת וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים עַל־ הַלְּבֵנִֽים׃ הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בַּקְּבָרִ֔ים וּבַנְּצוּרִ֖ים יָלִ֑ינוּ הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר הַחֲזִ֔יר וּפְרַק פִּגֻּלִ֖ים כְּלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They say, ‘Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!’ Such people are smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about a certain group of people.
These people say to others, "Stay away from me."
They say, "Do not come near me."
They claim, "I am holier than you."
God describes these people as offensive to Him.
God says, "These people are like smoke in My nostrils."
God says, "They are like a fire that burns all day long."
passages.original: הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ קְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־ תִּגַּשׁ־ בִּ֖י כִּ֣י קְדַשְׁתִּ֑יךָ אֵ֚לֶּה עָשָׁ֣ן בְּאַפִּ֔י אֵ֥שׁ יֹקֶ֖דֶת כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Behold, it is written before Me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will pay it back into their laps, both for your iniquities and for those of your fathers,” says the LORD. “Because they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Me on the hills, I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
He says, “I see everything.
It is written before Me.
I will not keep silent.
I will repay.
I will pay back into their laps.
I will repay you for your sins.
I will repay you for the sins of your fathers.
You burned incense on the mountains.
You scorned Me on the hills.
I will give you full payment for your former deeds.
I will measure it into your laps.”
passages.original: הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י לֹ֤א אֶחֱשֶׂה֙ כִּ֣י אִם־ שִׁלַּ֔מְתִּי וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֖י עַל־ חֵיקָֽם׃ עֲ֠וֺנֹתֵיכֶם וַעֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ עַל־ הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים וְעַל־ הַגְּבָע֖וֹת חֵרְפ֑וּנִי וּמַדֹּתִ֧י פְעֻלָּתָ֛ם רִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה עַל חֵיקָֽם׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “As the new wine is found in a cluster of grapes, and men say, ‘Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing,’ so I will act on behalf of My servants; I will not destroy them all.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is just and merciful.
The LORD compares His actions to a cluster of grapes.
People find new wine in a cluster of grapes.
People say, “Do not destroy this cluster.”
They say this because there is a blessing in it.
The LORD says He will act the same way for His servants.
The LORD will not destroy all His people.
The LORD will spare His servants for the sake of the blessing among them.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א הַתִּירוֹשׁ֙ בָּֽאֶשְׁכּ֔וֹל וְאָמַר֙ אַל־ תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה בּ֑וֹ כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדַ֔י לְבִלְתִּ֖י הַֽשְׁחִ֥ית הַכֹּֽל׃

passages.text: And I will bring forth descendants from Jacob, and heirs from Judah; My elect will possess My mountains, and My servants will dwell there.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will bring forth descendants from Jacob.
The LORD will bring forth heirs from Judah.
The LORD’s chosen people will possess His mountains.
The LORD’s servants will live there.
passages.original: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י מִֽיַּעֲקֹב֙ זֶ֔רַע וּמִיהוּדָ֖ה יוֹרֵ֣שׁ הָרָ֑י וִירֵשׁ֣וּהָ בְחִירַ֔י וַעֲבָדַ֖י יִשְׁכְּנוּ־ שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for My people who seek Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God promises a blessing to those who seek Him.
Sharon is a region.
Sharon will become a pasture for flocks.
The Valley of Achor is a place.
The Valley of Achor will become a resting place for herds.
God will do this for His people who seek Him.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ לִנְוֵה־ צֹ֔אן וְעֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְרֵ֣בֶץ בָּקָ֑ר לְעַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּרָשֽׁוּנִי׃

passages.text: But you who forsake the LORD, who forget My holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny, I will destine you for the sword, and you will all kneel down to be slaughtered, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen; you did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”
passages.sermon:
You have forsaken the LORD.
You have forgotten God's holy mountain.
You prepare a table for Fortune.
You fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny.
God will appoint you for the sword.
All of you will kneel to be slaughtered.
God called you, but you did not answer.
God spoke to you, but you did not listen.
You did evil in God's sight.
You chose what God did not desire.
passages.original: וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹזְבֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הַשְּׁכֵחִ֖ים אֶת־ הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֑י הַֽעֹרְכִ֤ים לַגַּד֙ שֻׁלְחָ֔ן וְהַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים לַמְנִ֥י מִמְסָֽךְ׃ וּמָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם לַחֶ֗רֶב וְכֻלְּכֶם֙ לַטֶּ֣בַח תִּכְרָ֔עוּ יַ֤עַן קָרָ֙אתִי֙ וְלֹ֣א עֲנִיתֶ֔ם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וַתַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ חָפַ֖צְתִּי בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃פ

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: “My servants will eat, but you will go hungry; My servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks with authority.
He addresses two groups of people.
The first group is His servants.
His servants are those who seek Him and obey Him.
The second group is those who forsake Him.
He makes a clear promise to His servants.
His servants will eat.
The other group will go hungry.
His servants will drink.
The other group will go thirsty.
His servants will rejoice.
The other group will be put to shame.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־ אָמַ֣ר׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י׀ יֹאכֵ֙לוּ֙ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּרְעָ֔בוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׁתּ֖וּ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּצְמָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׂמָ֖חוּ וְאַתֶּ֥ם תֵּבֹֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: My servants will shout for joy with a glad heart, but you will cry out with a heavy heart and wail with a broken spirit.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to those who forsake Him and forget His holy mountain.
He calls some people His servants.
His servants will shout for joy.
Their hearts will be glad.
But you who reject the Lord will cry out.
Your hearts will be full of pain.
You will wail with a broken spirit.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יָרֹ֖נּוּ מִטּ֣וּב לֵ֑ב וְאַתֶּ֤ם תִּצְעֲקוּ֙ מִכְּאֵ֣ב לֵ֔ב וּמִשֵּׁ֥בֶר ר֖וּחַ תְּיֵלִֽילוּ׃

passages.text: You will leave behind your name as a curse for My chosen ones, and the Lord GOD will slay you; but to His servants He will give another name.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks with authority.
He addresses those who reject Him.
You will leave your name behind.
Your name will become a curse among My chosen people.
The Lord GOD will put you to death.
He will give His servants a new name.
passages.original: וְהִנַּחְתֶּ֨ם שִׁמְכֶ֤ם לִשְׁבוּעָה֙ לִבְחִירַ֔י וֶהֱמִיתְךָ֖ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְלַעֲבָדָ֥יו יִקְרָ֖א שֵׁ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃

passages.text: Whoever invokes a blessing in the land will do so by the God of truth, and whoever takes an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth. For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of truth.
People in the land will bless others by the God of truth.
People in the land will swear oaths by the God of truth.
God will cause former troubles to be forgotten.
God will hide past troubles from His sight.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַמִּתְבָּרֵ֜ךְ בָּאָ֗רֶץ יִתְבָּרֵךְ֙ בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֔ן וְהַנִּשְׁבָּ֣ע בָּאָ֔רֶץ יִשָּׁבַ֖ע בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֑ן כִּ֣י נִשְׁכְּח֗וּ הַצָּרוֹת֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְכִ֥י נִסְתְּר֖וּ מֵעֵינָֽי׃

passages.text: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, “I will create new heavens.
I will create a new earth.
People will not remember the former things.
The former things will not come into anyone’s mind.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִזָּכַ֙רְנָה֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְלֹ֥א תַעֲלֶ֖ינָה עַל־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: But be glad and rejoice forever in what I create; for I will create Jerusalem to be a joy and its people to be a delight.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God commands them to be glad.
God commands them to rejoice forever.
God tells them to rejoice in what He creates.
God says, “I will create Jerusalem.”
God will make Jerusalem a place of joy.
God will make the people of Jerusalem a delight.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אִם־ שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְגִ֙ילוּ֙ עֲדֵי־ עַ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם גִּילָ֖ה וְעַמָּ֥הּ מָשֽׂוֹשׂ׃

passages.text: I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people. The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her.
passages.sermon:
God speaks.
God will rejoice in Jerusalem.
God will take delight in His people.
No one will hear weeping in Jerusalem.
No one will hear crying in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְגַלְתִּ֥י בִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְשַׂשְׂתִּ֣י בְעַמִּ֑י וְלֹֽא־ יִשָּׁמַ֥ע בָּהּ֙ ע֔וֹד ק֥וֹל בְּכִ֖י וְק֥וֹל זְעָקָֽה׃

passages.text: No longer will a nursing infant live but a few days, or an old man fail to live out his years. For the youth will die at a hundred years, and he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed.
passages.sermon:
God creates a new Jerusalem.
God makes Jerusalem a place of joy.
God makes the people of Jerusalem a delight.
In this new Jerusalem, infants will not die young.
No baby will live only a few days.
Old men will not die before their time.
Every old man will live out all his years.
A young person will live to be one hundred years old.
If someone dies before one hundred, people will call him accursed.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה מִשָּׁ֜ם ע֗וֹד ע֤וּל יָמִים֙ וְזָקֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת־ יָמָ֑יו כִּ֣י הַנַּ֗עַר בֶּן־ מֵאָ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יָמ֔וּת וְהַ֣חוֹטֶ֔א בֶּן־ מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה יְקֻלָּֽל׃

passages.text: They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people.
His people will build houses.
They will live in the houses they build.
They will plant vineyards.
They will eat the fruit from their own vineyards.
passages.original: וּבָנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְיָשָׁ֑בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְאָכְל֖וּ פִּרְיָֽם׃

passages.text: No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat. For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people, and My chosen ones will fully enjoy the work of their hands.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people.
God promises a new time for His people.
His people will build houses.
They will live in the houses they build.
They will plant crops and vineyards.
They will eat the food they grow.
No one else will take their houses.
No one else will eat their harvest.
God says His people will live long lives.
Their lives will be like the days of a tree.
God’s chosen people will enjoy their own work.
They will fully benefit from what they do.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יִבְנוּ֙ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֵשֵׁ֔ב לֹ֥א יִטְּע֖וּ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ כִימֵ֤י הָעֵץ֙ יְמֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַלּ֥וּ בְחִירָֽי׃

passages.text: They will not labor in vain or bear children doomed to disaster; for they will be a people blessed by the LORD— they and their descendants with them.
passages.sermon:
God’s people will not work for nothing.
They will not have children who face disaster.
God will bless these people.
God will bless their children too.
God’s blessing will remain with them and their descendants.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יִֽיגְעוּ֙ לָרִ֔יק וְלֹ֥א יֵלְד֖וּ לַבֶּהָלָ֑ה כִּ֣י זֶ֜רַע בְּרוּכֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּֽם׃

passages.text: Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD listens to His people.
Before they call, the LORD answers.
While they are still speaking, the LORD hears.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֥ה טֶֽרֶם־ יִקְרָ֖אוּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶעֱנֶ֑ה ע֛וֹד הֵ֥ם מְדַבְּרִ֖ים וַאֲנִ֥י אֶשְׁמָֽע׃

passages.text: The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, but the food of the serpent will be dust. They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain,” says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says what will happen on His holy mountain.
The wolf will feed together with the lamb.
The lion will eat straw like the ox.
The serpent will eat dust for its food.
No one will harm on God’s holy mountain.
No one will destroy on God’s holy mountain.
passages.original: זְאֵ֨ב וְטָלֶ֜ה יִרְע֣וּ כְאֶחָ֗ד וְאַרְיֵה֙ כַּבָּקָ֣ר יֹֽאכַל־ תֶּ֔בֶן וְנָחָ֖שׁ עָפָ֣ר לַחְמ֑וֹ לֹֽא־ יָרֵ֧עוּ וְלֹֽא־ יַשְׁחִ֛יתוּ בְּכָל־ הַ֥ר קָדְשִׁ֖י אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס
